source: hand-computed from the field layouts; FECFs independently recomputed with a reference CRC-16-CCITT
note: AOS transfer frames. Each vector isolates the primary header fields and the optional error control fields so a packing error names the field rather than hiding in a whole frame. The FHEC vectors are marked unverified; their notes say exactly what is and is not established.

encode.name: frame-with-fecf
encode.note: TFVN=01, SCID=0xab, VCID=42, VCFC=0x000102, replay=0, VCFC usage=1, cycle=3. byte 0 = 01<<6 | 0xab>>2 = 0x6a; byte 1 = (0xab&0x3)<<6 | 42 = 0xea; bytes 2-4 = 00 01 02; byte 5 = 0x40 | 0x03 = 0x43. FECF is CRC-16-CCITT (poly 0x1021, init 0xffff) over the whole frame = 0x9e2c, computed with an independent implementation.

encode.name: frame-with-fhec-and-fecf
encode.note: Frame with both header and frame error control. The FHEC occupies bits 48-63 of the primary header, per clause 4.1.2.6.1, and the FECF follows the data field. The FHEC value ce8e is the RS(10,6) check over the header, derived below.

decode.name: frame-with-fecf-inverse
decode.note: The inverse of the frame-with-fecf encode vector. Reads back every primary header field from the same octets.

decode.name: frame-with-fhec-inverse
decode.note: The inverse of the FHEC frame: the two FHEC octets are read back and the data field starts after them, so a decoder that treats the primary header as a fixed six octets when the channel carries an FHEC reads the check symbols as data.

decode.name: fhec-of-primary-header
decode.note: The RS(10,6) frame header error control over the primary header 6aea00010243. Clause 4.1.2.6.5 c) gives the field generator F(x) = x^4 + x + 1 over GF(2), and d) the code generator g(x) = x^4 + a^3 x^3 + a x^2 + a^3 x + 1 over GF(2^4). The bit-to-symbol mapping in f) makes the six information symbols header bits 0-15 and 40-47, which for this header are the nibbles 6, a, e, a, 4, 3 -- the 24-bit VC frame count in bits 16-39 is deliberately not protected. Systematic encoding gives check symbols c, e, 8, e, so the field is ce8e.

reject.name: signaling-field-spare-bits-set
reject.note: Bits 42-43 of the primary header are the signalling field's reserved spare, and clause 4.1.2.5.4.2 requires them to be zero. byte 5 = 0x73 sets them; a conforming decoder refuses the frame rather than ignoring them.

reject.name: header-truncated
reject.note: Two octets cannot hold the 6-octet primary header. A decoder must not get past octet 2: the primary header is 6 octets; the input stops after 2.

reject.name: vc-frame-count-above-twenty-four-bit-field
reject.note: 2^24 does not fit the 24-bit VC frame count field. It must be refused rather than masked: a frame count is how a receiver detects gaps, so substituting 0 for an out-of-range value reads as a lost frame rather than a caller mistake.

reject.name: vc-frame-count-cycle-above-four-bit-field
reject.note: The VC frame count cycle is bits 44-47 of the primary header, four bits inside the signalling field, so 16 does not fit. Masking it would silently report a different cycle and share octet 5 with the flags beside it.

reject.name: virtual-channel-id-above-six-bit-field
reject.note: 64 does not fit the 6-bit VCID field; it would overflow into the bit beside it.
